description: A soft preparation rubbed into book leather to nourish it and keep it flexible. A serviceable mixture is made by warming a quantity of oil with roughly half its weight of shredded wax until the wax melts. It must not stain, evaporate quickly, harden, or stay sticky; Cockerell prefers a wax-in-oil dressing over plain petroleum jelly, which evaporates slowly.
name: leather dressing

source_ref.label: Douglas Cockerell, Bookbinding and the Care of Books (D. Appleton, 1901), Internet Archive
